name: Belial
role: Infernal council voice for inaction / despair dressed as prudence
description: Category A+B: in Hebrew, 'Belial' (beliyya'al, 'worthlessness') is overwhelmingly an idiom, not a name -- 'sons of Belial' means scoundrels (Deuteronomy 13:13, Judges 19:22). Personifies into an actual named arch-demon later in the Dead Sea Scrolls (Community Rule, War Scroll -- commands the 'Sons of Darkness') and 2 Corinthians 6:15. Milton's smooth-talking, cowardly, hedonistic advocate of 'ignoble ease' in the Book II debate is personality invented wholesale (D) on the bare demonic name. See docs/milton/character-catalog.md §II.
narrative_function: Argues for passive endurance in the Book II council -- the self-pity/despair voice the book's thesis contrasts against Satan's actual choice to act.
